subproblem.title: Slice bound on a convex set: ∫⁻_Q∫⁻_Q g((1 − t)y + tx) ≤ 2ⁿ Lⁿ(Q) ∫⁻_Q g
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ := Euclid n with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ (volume), Q ⊆ ℝⁿ convex and measurable, g : ℝⁿ → [0, ∞] measurable, and t ∈ [0, 1]. Then ∫⁻_{x∈Q} ∫⁻_{y∈Q} g((1 − t)y + tx) dy dx ≤ 2ⁿ · Lⁿ(Q) · ∫⁻_Q g. All integrals are lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, ∞] (outer variable x, inner variable y), and the right side is computed in [0, ∞] with 0 · ∞ = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Q : Set (Euclid n)) (g : Euclid n → ℝ≥0∞), Convex ℝ Q → MeasurableSet Q → Measurable g → ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x) ≤ 2 ^ n * volume Q * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–4 of the parent proof.
- For t ∈ [1/2, 1], change variables in one variable; the Jacobian is tⁿ.
- For t ∈ [0, 1/2), swap the order of integration and change variables in the other variable; the Jacobian is (1 − t)ⁿ.
- In both cases the image lies in Q by convexity, and the reciprocal of the Jacobian factor is at most 2ⁿ.

Here this is stated for an arbitrary convex measurable Q and a measurable g : ℝⁿ → [0, ∞], in lower-Lebesgue-integral form, so Tonelli needs no integrability hypothesis. The variables are named so that the inner variable y carries the weight 1 − t: the integrand is g((1 − t)y + tx). The same argument for Q = unit ball is the accepted Lean proof of Submission.dorag_ha_pb_slice_bound (commit 7ad779ea2).

Notation. ℝⁿ := Euclid n and Lⁿ := volume. ∫⁻ denotes lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, ∞], and products are taken in [0, ∞] with 0·∞ = 0. Fix t ∈ [0, 1].

1. One-variable bound. Claim: if c ∈ ℝⁿ, s ≥ 1/2, and c + s·v ∈ Q for every v ∈ Q, then ∫⁻_{v∈Q} g(c + s·v) dv ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g.
   Proof of the claim. Note s > 0. Let F := 1_Q·g, the extension of g|Q by 0; F is measurable because g and Q are.
   (a) For v ∈ Q we have c + s·v ∈ Q, so g(c + s·v) = F(c + s·v). Hence
       ∫⁻_{v∈Q} g(c + s·v) dv = ∫⁻_{v∈Q} F(c + s·v) dv ≤ ∫⁻_{ℝⁿ} F(c + s·v) dv.
   (b) The image of Lⁿ under the dilation v ↦ s·v is ofReal|s^{−n}|·Lⁿ = s^{−n}·Lⁿ (Measure.map_addHaar_smul, with finrank ℝ (Euclid n) = n, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Therefore
       ∫⁻ F(c + s·v) dv = ∫⁻ F(c + w) d(map)(w) = s^{−n} ∫⁻ F(c + w) dw
       (lintegral_map, lintegral_smul_measure). By translation invariance of Lⁿ (lintegral_add_left_eq_self), this equals s^{−n} ∫⁻ F = s^{−n} ∫⁻_Q g (lintegral_indicator).
   (c) s ≥ 1/2 gives s^{−1} ≤ 2, hence ofReal(s^{−n}) = ofReal(s^{−1})ⁿ ≤ 2ⁿ.
   Combining (a)–(c) proves the claim.
2. Joint measurability. (x, y) ↦ g((1 − t)y + tx) is measurable on ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ: it is the measurable g composed with a continuous map.
3. Case t ≥ 1/2. By Tonelli for the s-finite measures Lⁿ restricted to Q (lintegral_lintegral_swap, using step 2),
   ∫⁻_{x∈Q} ∫⁻_{y∈Q} g((1 − t)y + tx) dy dx = ∫⁻_{y∈Q} ∫⁻_{x∈Q} g((1 − t)y + tx) dx dy.
   Fix y ∈ Q and apply step 1 with c := (1 − t)y and s := t ≥ 1/2. For x ∈ Q, c + t·x = (1 − t)y + tx lies in Q by convexity (weights 1 − t ≥ 0 and t ≥ 0 with sum 1). So the inner integral is ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g for every y ∈ Q. By monotonicity of the set integral over the measurable set Q (setLIntegral_mono') and setLIntegral_const, the whole expression is
   ≤ ∫⁻_{y∈Q} 2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g = (2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g)·Lⁿ(Q) = 2ⁿ·Lⁿ(Q)·∫⁻_Q g.
4. Case t ≤ 1/2. Fix x ∈ Q. Since (1 − t)y + tx = tx + (1 − t)y, apply step 1 with c := tx and s := 1 − t ≥ 1/2. For y ∈ Q, tx + (1 − t)y lies in Q by convexity. So ∫⁻_{y∈Q} g((1 − t)y + tx) dy ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g for every x ∈ Q. Integrating this constant bound over x ∈ Q exactly as in step 3 gives ≤ 2ⁿ·Lⁿ(Q)·∫⁻_Q g.
5. Every t ∈ [0, 1] satisfies t ≥ 1/2 or t ≤ 1/2, so steps 3–4 prove the statement. Finiteness of Lⁿ(Q) and of ∫⁻_Q g is never used: every step is an inequality in [0, ∞]. ∎

  intro n Q g hQc hQm hg t ht
  obtain ⟨ht0, ht1⟩ := ht
  have key : ∀ (c : Euclid n) (s : ℝ), 1 / 2 ≤ s →
      (∀ v ∈ Q, c + s • v ∈ Q) →
      ∫⁻ v in Q, g (c + s • v) ≤ 2 ^ n * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
    intro c s hs hcs
    have hs0 : 0 < s := by linarith
    obtain ⟨F, hFdef⟩ : ∃ F : Euclid n → ℝ≥0∞, F = Q.indicator g := ⟨_, rfl⟩
    have hF : Measurable F := hFdef ▸ hg.indicator hQm
    have hcv : ∫⁻ v, F (c + s • v) = ENNReal.ofReal |(s ^ n)⁻¹| * ∫⁻ z, F z := by
      have h1 : ∫⁻ w, F (c + w) ∂(Measure.map (fun v : Euclid n => s • v) volume)
          = ∫⁻ v, F (c + s • v) :=
        lintegral_map (hF.comp (measurable_const_add c)) (measurable_const_smul s)
      rw [← h1, Measure.map_addHaar_smul volume hs0.ne', lintegral_smul_measure,
        lintegral_add_left_eq_self F c, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, smul_eq_mul]
    have hs2 : s⁻¹ ≤ 2 := by
      rw [inv_le_comm₀ hs0 two_pos]
      linarith
    calc ∫⁻ v in Q, g (c + s • v)
        = ∫⁻ v in Q, F (c + s • v) := by
          refine setLIntegral_congr_fun hQm fun v hv => ?_
          rw [hFdef, Set.indicator_of_mem (hcs v hv)]
      _ ≤ ∫⁻ v, F (c + s • v) := setLIntegral_le_lintegral _ _
      _ = ENNReal.ofReal |(s ^ n)⁻¹| * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
          rw [hcv, hFdef, lintegral_indicator hQm]
      _ ≤ 2 ^ n * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
          gcongr
          calc ENNReal.ofReal |(s ^ n)⁻¹| = ENNReal.ofReal s⁻¹ ^ n := by
                rw [abs_of_pos (by positivity), ← inv_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_pow (by positivity)]
            _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal 2 ^ n := by gcongr
            _ = 2 ^ n := by rw [ENNReal.ofReal_ofNat]
  have hmeas : Measurable (fun p : Euclid n × Euclid n => g ((1 - t) • p.2 + t • p.1)) :=
    hg.comp (by fun_prop)

  · rw [lintegral_lintegral_swap (f := fun x y => g ((1 - t) • y + t • x)) hmeas.aemeasurable]
    calc ∫⁻ y in Q, ∫⁻ x in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x)

          refine setLIntegral_mono' hQm fun y hy => ?_

          rw [setLIntegral_const]
          ring
  · calc ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x)
        ≤ ∫⁻ _ in Q, 2 ^ n * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
          refine setLIntegral_mono' hQm fun x hx => ?_

              = ∫⁻ y in Q, g (t • x + (1 - t) • y) :=
                lintegral_congr fun y => by rw [add_comm]
            _ ≤ 2 ^ n * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
                refine key (t • x) (1 - t) (by linarith) fun v hv => ?_
                rw [add_comm]

          rw [setLIntegral_const]

subproblem.title: Geometry of the cube Q_δ: convex, measurable, diameter ≤ √n, volume ≤ 1
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, δ ≥ 0, and Q_δ := {z ∈ Euclid n : δ < z_i < 1 − δ for all i}. Then Q_δ is convex, Q_δ is measurable, ‖x − y‖ ≤ √n for all x, y ∈ Q_δ, and Lⁿ(Q_δ) ≤ 1 (Lebesgue measure volume, as an element of [0, ∞]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (δ : ℝ), 0 ≤ δ → Convex ℝ {z : Euclid n | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ} ∧ MeasurableSet {z : Euclid n | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ} ∧ (∀ x ∈ {z : Euclid n | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ∀ y ∈ {z : Euclid n | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ‖x - y‖ ≤ Real.sqrt n) ∧ volume {z : Euclid n | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ} ≤ 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 and the Notation paragraph of the parent proof:
- Q_δ is open, convex and bounded;
- |x − y| ≤ √n·s with s = 1 − 2δ ≤ 1;
- under the measure-preserving coordinate map Euclid n → (Fin n → ℝ), Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ).

Only the coarser consequences ‖x − y‖ ≤ √n and Lⁿ(Q_δ) ≤ 1 are recorded. They hold for every δ ≥ 0, so the parent's case distinction δ ≥ 1/2 (empty cube) is not needed.

Notation. Q_δ := {z ∈ Euclid n : δ < z_i < 1 − δ for all i}, where z_i = z.ofLp i is the i-th coordinate. Lⁿ := volume on Euclid n.

1. Convexity. By convex_iff_forall_pos it suffices to take x, y ∈ Q_δ and a, b > 0 with a + b = 1. For each i, (a·x + b·y)_i = a·x_i + b·y_i, and
   a·x_i + b·y_i − δ = a(x_i − δ) + b(y_i − δ) > 0,
   (1 − δ) − (a·x_i + b·y_i) = a(1 − δ − x_i) + b(1 − δ − y_i) > 0,
   since each term is a product of two positive numbers. Hence a·x + b·y ∈ Q_δ.
2. Measurability. Q_δ = ⋂_i ({z : δ < z_i} ∩ {z : z_i < 1 − δ}). Each coordinate map z ↦ z_i is continuous, hence measurable, so each set {z : δ < z_i} and {z : z_i < 1 − δ} is measurable (measurableSet_lt). The finite intersection is then measurable (MeasurableSet.iInter, MeasurableSet.inter).
3. Diameter. Let x, y ∈ Q_δ. For each i, δ < x_i, y_i < 1 − δ gives −1 ≤ −(1 − 2δ) < x_i − y_i < 1 − 2δ ≤ 1 (using δ ≥ 0), so (x_i − y_i)² ≤ 1. Hence ‖x − y‖ = √(∑_i (x_i − y_i)²) ≤ √(∑_i 1) = √n (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and monotonicity of √).

subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ := Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), v : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 v), and x, y ∈ ℝⁿ. Then |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ ‖x − y‖ · ∫_0^1 ‖Dv((1 − t)y + tx)‖ dt, where Dv(z) = fderiv ℝ v z with the operator norm and the integral is the interval integral from 0 to 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (v : Euclid n → ℝ) (x y : Euclid n), ContDiff ℝ 1 v → |v x - v y| ≤ ‖x - y‖ * ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖fderiv ℝ v ((1 - t) • y + t • x)‖

Source: step 1 (segment estimate) of the parent proof. Here it is stated for all x, y ∈ ℝⁿ and without the diameter bound, which the consumer convex_poincare applies itself (‖x − y‖ ≤ d). The segment is parametrized as p(t) = (1 − t)y + tx, so p(0) = y and p(1) = x.

Notation. ℝⁿ := Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Dv(z) := fderiv ℝ v z ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝ), with the operator norm. ∫_0^1 is the interval integral.

1. Regularity. v is C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 v with 1 ≠ 0). So v is differentiable at every point, HasFDerivAt v (Dv(z)) z holds for all z, and z ↦ Dv(z) is continuous.
2. The segment. Let p(t) := (1 − t)y + tx for t ∈ ℝ. Then p is continuous, p(0) = y and p(1) = x. Its derivative at every t is (−1)·y + 1·x = x − y.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0, 2 and 5 of the parent proof (finiteness; integrating the segment estimate over Q × Q with Tonelli; the final estimate), for a general convex measurable Q with ‖x − y‖ ≤ d on Q.
- Step 1 of the parent proof is the sibling segment_bound (Submission.cmcdt_cbm_sp_segment_bound).
- Steps 3–4 of the parent proof are the sibling convex_slice_bound (Submission.cmcdt_cbm_sp_convex_slice_bound).

The bound keeps the factors d and Lⁿ(Q) separate; the parent later uses d = √n and Lⁿ(Q) ≤ 1. The structure is that of the accepted Lean proof of Submission.dorag_ha_pb_double_integral_bound (commit cba007e5f), without the square.

Notation. ℝⁿ := Euclid n and Lⁿ := volume. F(z) := ‖Dv(z)‖ = ‖fderiv ℝ v z‖ and g(z) := ofReal(F(z)) ∈ [0, ∞). ∫⁻ are lower Lebesgue integrals; ∫ are Bochner integrals.

1. Regularity and finiteness.
   - v is continuous, and F is continuous because v is C¹ (so Dv is continuous).
   - Q is bounded, since dist(x, y) = ‖x − y‖ ≤ d for x, y ∈ Q (Metric.isBounded_iff). Hence Lⁿ(Q) < ∞ (Bornology.IsBounded.measure_lt_top) and closure(Q) is compact.
   - So there is C with F(z) ≤ C for z ∈ closure(Q) ⊇ Q (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn).
   - g is measurable, and ∫⁻_Q g ≤ ∫⁻_Q ofReal(C) = ofReal(C)·Lⁿ(Q) < ∞.
2. Pointwise bound. Fix x, y ∈ Q and let G := ∫_0^1 F((1 − t)y + tx) dt ≥ 0 (interval integral).
   - By segment_bound, |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ ‖x − y‖·G ≤ d·G, using ‖x − y‖ ≤ d and G ≥ 0.
   - Since 0 ≤ 1, G = ∫_{(0,1]} F((1 − t)y + tx) dt (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le). The integrand is nonnegative and continuous, so G = toReal(∫⁻_{t∈(0,1]} g((1 − t)y + tx) dt) (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae). Hence ofReal(G) ≤ ∫⁻_{t∈(0,1]} g((1 − t)y + tx) dt, because ofReal(toReal a) ≤ a.
   - As d ≥ 0, ofReal|v(x) − v(y)| ≤ ofReal(d·G) = ofReal(d)·ofReal(G) ≤ ofReal(d)·∫⁻_{t∈(0,1]} g((1 − t)y + tx) dt.
3. Tonelli.
   - For fixed x, (y, t) ↦ g((1 − t)y + tx) is measurable: it is g composed with a continuous map.
   - (x, t) ↦ ∫⁻_{y∈Q} g((1 − t)y + tx) dy is measurable: it is a parametric lower integral of the jointly measurable function ((x, t), y) ↦ g((1 − t)y + tx) (Measurable.lintegral_prod_right').
   - Two applications of Tonelli (lintegral_lintegral_swap) give
     ∫⁻_{x∈Q} ∫⁻_{y∈Q} ∫⁻_{t∈(0,1]} g((1 − t)y + tx) = ∫⁻_{t∈(0,1]} ∫⁻_{x∈Q} ∫⁻_{y∈Q} g((1 − t)y + tx).
4. Lower-integral estimate. Integrate step 2 over y ∈ Q and then over x ∈ Q (setLIntegral_mono'). Pull out the finite constant ofReal(d) (lintegral_const_mul') and use step 3. Then bound each t-slice by convex_slice_bound, applied to Q, g and t ∈ (0, 1] ⊆ [0, 1]. Since L¹((0, 1]) = 1, this gives
   ∫⁻_{x∈Q} ∫⁻_{y∈Q} ofReal|v(x) − v(y)| ≤ ofReal(d)·∫⁻_{t∈(0,1]} 2ⁿ·Lⁿ(Q)·∫⁻_Q g dt = ofReal(d)·(2ⁿ·Lⁿ(Q)·∫⁻_Q g) =: K.
   By step 1, K < ∞.
5. Back to Bochner integrals.
   (a) For every x, ∫_{y∈Q} |v(x) − v(y)| dy = toReal(h(x)), where h(x) := ∫⁻_{y∈Q} ofReal|v(x) − v(y)| dy (nonnegative continuous integrand; integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae).
   (b) h is measurable (Measurable.lintegral_prod_right', applied to the continuous map (x, y) ↦ |v(x) − v(y)|). So ∫_{x∈Q} toReal(h(x)) dx = toReal(∫⁻_{x∈Q} ofReal(toReal(h(x))) dx).
   (c) Since ofReal(toReal(h(x))) ≤ h(x), the last lower integral is ≤ ∫⁻_{x∈Q} h(x) dx ≤ K < ∞ by step 4. Monotonicity of toReal on finite values (ENNReal.toReal_mono) gives ∫_{x∈Q} ∫_{y∈Q} |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ toReal(K).
   (d) toReal(K) = d·2ⁿ·toReal(Lⁿ(Q))·toReal(∫⁻_Q g), because toReal is multiplicative and toReal(ofReal d) = d for d ≥ 0. Also toReal(∫⁻_Q g) = ∫_Q F, since F ≥ 0 is continuous.
   Therefore ∫_{x∈Q} ∫_{y∈Q} |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ 2ⁿ·d·Lⁿ(Q)·∫_Q ‖Dv‖. ∎

theorem Submission.cmcdt_cbm_sp_convex_poincare : ∀ (n : ℕ) (Q : Set (Euclid n)) (v : Euclid n → ℝ) (d : ℝ), Convex ℝ Q → MeasurableSet Q → 0 ≤ d → (∀ x ∈ Q, ∀ y ∈ Q, ‖x - y‖ ≤ d) → ContDiff ℝ 1 v → ∫ x in Q, ∫ y in Q, |v x - v y| ≤ 2 ^ n * d * (volume Q).toReal * ∫ z in Q, ‖fderiv ℝ v z‖ := by
  intro n Q v d hQc hQm hd hdiam hv
  have hseg := Submission.cmcdt_cbm_sp_segment_bound n v
  have hslice := Submission.cmcdt_cbm_sp_convex_slice_bound n Q
  have hcont : Continuous v := hv.continuous
  have hFc : Continuous fun z => ‖fderiv ℝ v z‖ := (hv.continuous_fderiv one_ne_zero).norm
  have hQb : Bornology.IsBounded Q :=
    Metric.isBounded_iff.2 ⟨d, fun x hx y hy => by rw [dist_eq_norm]; exact hdiam x hx y hy⟩
  have hQfin : volume Q < ∞ := hQb.measure_lt_top
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ : ∃ C, ∀ z ∈ closure Q, ‖‖fderiv ℝ v z‖‖ ≤ C :=
    hQb.isCompact_closure.exists_bound_of_continuousOn hFc.continuousOn
  obtain ⟨g, hg_def⟩ : ∃ g : Euclid n → ℝ≥0∞, g = fun z => ENNReal.ofReal ‖fderiv ℝ v z‖ :=
    ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have hgx : ∀ z, g z = ENNReal.ofReal ‖fderiv ℝ v z‖ := fun z => congrFun hg_def z
  have hg : Measurable g := hg_def ▸ hFc.measurable.ennreal_ofReal
  have hJ : ∫⁻ z in Q, g z ≠ ∞ := by
    have h1 : ∫⁻ z in Q, g z ≤ ∫⁻ _ in Q, ENNReal.ofReal C :=
      setLIntegral_mono' hQm fun z hz => by
        rw [hgx]
        exact ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (by simpa using hC z (subset_closure hz))
    rw [setLIntegral_const] at h1
    exact (h1.trans_lt (ENNReal.mul_lt_top ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top hQfin)).ne
  have hpt : ∀ x ∈ Q, ∀ y ∈ Q, ENNReal.ofReal |v x - v y| ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal d * ∫⁻ t in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x) := by
    intro x hx y hy
    set G := ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖fderiv ℝ v ((1 - t) • y + t • x)‖ with hG_def
    have hG : 0 ≤ G := intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg zero_le_one fun t _ => norm_nonneg _
    have h1 : |v x - v y| ≤ d * G :=
      (hseg x y hv).trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hdiam x hx y hy) hG)
    have hmt : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun t : ℝ => ‖fderiv ℝ v ((1 - t) • y + t • x)‖)
        (volume.restrict (Ioc 0 1)) := by
      have h : Continuous fun t : ℝ => (1 - t) • y + t • x := by fun_prop
      exact (hFc.comp h).aestronglyMeasurable
    have hGle : ENNReal.ofReal G ≤ ∫⁻ t in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x) := by
      rw [hG_def, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le zero_le_one,
        integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae (ae_of_all _ fun t => norm_nonneg _) hmt]
      simp only [hgx]
      exact ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le
    calc ENNReal.ofReal |v x - v y| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (d * G) := ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal h1
      _ = ENNReal.ofReal d * ENNReal.ofReal G := ENNReal.ofReal_mul hd
      _ ≤ _ := by gcongr
  have hmeas_yt : ∀ x : Euclid n,
      Measurable (uncurry fun (y : Euclid n) (t : ℝ) => g ((1 - t) • y + t • x)) := fun x =>
    hg.comp (by fun_prop : Continuous fun p : Euclid n × ℝ => (1 - p.2) • p.1 + p.2 • x).measurable
  have hmeas_xt : Measurable (uncurry fun (x : Euclid n) (t : ℝ) =>
      ∫⁻ y in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x)) :=
    Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'
      (f := fun q : (Euclid n × ℝ) × Euclid n => g ((1 - q.1.2) • q.2 + q.1.2 • q.1.1))
      (hg.comp (by fun_prop : Continuous fun q : (Euclid n × ℝ) × Euclid n =>
        (1 - q.1.2) • q.2 + q.1.2 • q.1.1).measurable)
  have hswap : ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q, ∫⁻ t in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x) =
      ∫⁻ t in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x) := by
    calc _ = ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ t in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∫⁻ y in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x) :=
          lintegral_congr fun x => lintegral_lintegral_swap (hmeas_yt x).aemeasurable
      _ = _ := lintegral_lintegral_swap hmeas_xt.aemeasurable
  have hI : ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q, ENNReal.ofReal |v x - v y| ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal d * (2 ^ n * volume Q * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z) := by
    calc ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q, ENNReal.ofReal |v x - v y|
        ≤ ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q,
            ENNReal.ofReal d * ∫⁻ t in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x) :=
          setLIntegral_mono' hQm fun x hx => setLIntegral_mono' hQm fun y hy => hpt x hx y hy
      _ = ENNReal.ofReal d * ∫⁻ t in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q,
            g ((1 - t) • y + t • x) := by
          simp only [lintegral_const_mul' _ _ ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top]
          rw [hswap]
      _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal d * ∫⁻ _ in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, 2 ^ n * volume Q * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
          exact mul_le_mul_right (setLIntegral_mono' measurableSet_Ioc fun t ht =>
            hslice g hQc hQm hg t (Ioc_subset_Icc_self ht)) _
      _ = ENNReal.ofReal d * (2 ^ n * volume Q * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z) := by
          rw [setLIntegral_const, Real.volume_Ioc, sub_zero, ENNReal.ofReal_one, mul_one]
  have hK : Measurable fun x : Euclid n => ∫⁻ y in Q, ENNReal.ofReal |v x - v y| := by
    have h : Continuous fun p : Euclid n × Euclid n => |v p.1 - v p.2| := by fun_prop
    exact Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'
      (f := fun p : Euclid n × Euclid n => ENNReal.ofReal |v p.1 - v p.2|)
      h.measurable.ennreal_ofReal
  have hinner : ∀ x : Euclid n, ∫ y in Q, |v x - v y| =
      (∫⁻ y in Q, ENNReal.ofReal |v x - v y|).toReal := fun x =>
    integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae (ae_of_all _ fun y => abs_nonneg _)
      (by fun_prop : Continuous fun y => |v x - v y|).aestronglyMeasurable
  have hrhs : ∫ z in Q, ‖fderiv ℝ v z‖ = (∫⁻ z in Q, g z).toReal := by
    rw [integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae (ae_of_all _ fun z => norm_nonneg _)
      hFc.aestronglyMeasurable]
    simp only [hgx]
  have hfin : ENNReal.ofReal d * (2 ^ n * volume Q * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z) ≠ ∞ :=
    ENNReal.mul_ne_top ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top (ENNReal.mul_ne_top (ENNReal.mul_ne_top
      (ENNReal.pow_ne_top ENNReal.ofNat_ne_top) hQfin.ne) hJ)
  calc ∫ x in Q, ∫ y in Q, |v x - v y|
      = ∫ x in Q, (∫⁻ y in Q, ENNReal.ofReal |v x - v y|).toReal := by simp only [hinner]
    _ = (∫⁻ x in Q, ENNReal.ofReal (∫⁻ y in Q, ENNReal.ofReal |v x - v y|).toReal).toReal :=
        integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae (ae_of_all _ fun x => ENNReal.toReal_nonneg)
          hK.ennreal_toReal.aestronglyMeasurable
    _ ≤ (ENNReal.ofReal d * (2 ^ n * volume Q * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z)).toReal :=
        ENNReal.toReal_mono hfin ((lintegral_mono fun x => ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le).trans hI)
    _ = 2 ^ n * d * (volume Q).toReal * ∫ z in Q, ‖fderiv ℝ v z‖ := by
        rw [hrhs, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_pow,
          ENNReal.toReal_ofNat, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hd]
        ring
proof_key_steps: F = ‖Dv‖ is continuous; Q is bounded, so Lⁿ(Q) < ∞ and F ≤ C on Q; g = ofReal ∘ F has finite lower integral over Q.
segment_bound and ‖x − y‖ ≤ d: ofReal|v(x) − v(y)| ≤ ofReal(d)·∫⁻_{(0,1]} g((1 − t)y + tx) dt for x, y ∈ Q.
Tonelli moves the t-integral outside; convex_slice_bound bounds each t-slice by 2ⁿ Lⁿ(Q) ∫⁻_Q g.
Hence ∫⁻_Q∫⁻_Q ofReal|v(x) − v(y)| ≤ ofReal(d)·2ⁿ Lⁿ(Q) ∫⁻_Q g < ∞.
Convert to Bochner integrals (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae, toReal monotonicity) to get ≤ 2ⁿ d Lⁿ(Q) ∫_Q ‖Dv‖.

audit.reason: All hypotheses and the real-valued volume factor match the frozen type. The diameter bound gives boundedness and compact closure, establishing finiteness of the gradient lower integral. The two declared dependencies supply exactly the segment and slice estimates. Joint measurability, Tonelli and conversion to Bochner integrals are justified, with a finite upper bound established before applying toReal monotonicity. The proof is complete and non-circular.
